data.narrative:
Summit Lithium Technologies is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Amanda Hall that has raised approximately C$120M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector, comprising one public company and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The Stage-Progression method was the applicable triangulation approach for this analysis. Using the C$120M total capital raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of C$240M. The Peer-Median method was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data points within the Climate & Energy sector; while eight same-sector peers exist, fewer than three met the narrow filtering criteria necessary to produce a reliable median benchmark.

The analysis supports a valuation range of C$204M (low) to C$276M (high), with a median point of C$240M. This single-method result carries elevated uncertainty given reliance on stage-progression mechanics alone. Key uncertainties include the availability of closer-stage peer valuations in the emerging climate-tech market, capital efficiency relative to sector peers, and the specific technology stage and commercialization timeline of Summit's lithium platform.
